external_contracts: OSSL_STORE_LOADER_free: loader is NULL or a live loader this crate allocated, and the caller owns exactly one reference to it. A provider loader is released through RC-1/D562; a legacy loader (prov == NULL) releases the block directly and never touches the count.
OSSL_STORE_LOADER_up_ref: loader is live; a provider loader's positive count is incremented; the legacy arm answers 1 without a count, as the authority does.
The provider's OSSL_DISPATCH table is non-NULL, terminated by function_id == 0, and every present entry has the signature of the OSSL_FUNC_STORE_* id it names.
An OSSL_ALGORITHM supplied by the algorithm walk is live for the call; algorithm_names, property_definition and algorithm_description outlive the loader (the loader holds a provider reference).

The mcm callback contract of B22-MCM-1..4: put increments the method reference, a NULL store names the global store, the temporary store belongs to the mcm owner, and no callback re-enters the held store lock.
Do_all callbacks receive a borrowed loader; they must not release the store's reference without first acquiring their own via OSSL_STORE_LOADER_up_ref.
OSSL_STORE_LOADER_names_do_all callback names are borrowed from the name map and valid only for that callback.

boundaries.mechanism: loader object lifecycle: new_loader (zalloc, count-1 store, provider up-ref), CtxDestroy body, OSSL_STORE_LOADER_up_ref/free, up_ref_loader/free_loader
boundaries.contract: new_loader publishes a zeroed, valid OsslStoreLoader with count 1 and, on success, one provider reference; the failure arms release only what was acquired (no provider when the up-ref was refused; block only). OSSL_STORE_LOADER_free releases exactly one caller reference; a provider loader is freed by the Last down-ref under the REF_DESTROYING sentinel, a re-entrant free observes Retired, and a legacy loader releases the block directly.

boundaries.mechanism: dispatch scan, construction and destruction: loader_from_algorithm (ten OSSL_FUNC_STORE_* slots), construct_loader (namemap add, name map key is the scheme), destruct_loader
boundaries.contract: The first non-NULL function per id wins; the authority's four-clause sanity check (open|attach, load, eof, close; set_ctx_params optional) frees the partial loader and raises OSSL_STORE_R_LOADER_INCOMPLETE exactly once. construct_loader pairs with destruct_loader through the B22 mcm put/destruct refcount contract: construct answers 1 reference, put takes one, destruct drops the construction reference.

boundaries.mechanism: fetch plumbing: LoaderDataSt, get_tmp_loader_store/dealloc, reserve/unreserve, get_loader_from_store/put_loader_in_store bridges, inner_loader_fetch, OSSL_STORE_LOADER_fetch
boundaries.contract: The temporary store is created by get and released exactly once by the fetch/do_all owner; every loader returned to the caller carries one caller reference and every cached loader carries one cache reference. Lock order is biglock -> namemap/property lock; no user callback runs under either lock. The unsupported-vs-fetch-failed reason split and the dynamic error text match store_meth.c:346-369.
A missing slot-15 store answers 1 (the authority's answer); otherwise the call is forwarded to the method store under its own locks. The provider is used only by identity.

boundaries.mechanism: by-name accessors: get0_provider, get0_properties, get_number, get0_description, is_a, names_do_all, settable_ctx_params
boundaries.contract: Every returned provider/string/param pointer is borrowed from the loader or its provider and must not be freed. get0_provider/get0_properties/get_number guard NULL and raise the authority's PASSED_NULL_PARAMETER; get0_description does not guard, matching store_meth.c:440-443 and its live-loader contract. is_a compares the name-map number with scheme_id; names_do_all passes borrowed names and never holds the map lock across the callback.

The fetch fills the temporary store first; both stores are then walked through ossl_method_store_do_all, which snapshots under the read lock and invokes the visitor after releasing it. The visitor receives a borrowed loader and this file neither takes nor releases its reference; user_fn must be non-NULL.

escalations.class: double release / use-after-free under allocation failure
escalations.description: OSSL_STORE_open_ex's err tail calls OSSL_STORE_LOADER_free(fetched_loader) after ossl_store_close_it(&tmpctx) already released the context's reference (:665), when loader_ctx was non-NULL. The second call releases a reference the caller no longer owns; with the cache reference present it frees the block while the method-store Query still points at it, so the next cache hit or flush uses freed memory. The path is reachable when propq_copy (:887) or the OwnedCtx allocation (:896) is refused after a successful provider open. The authority reproduces the same release at store_lib.c:234 (Coverity-suppressed).
escalations.scope: Out of this one-file batch by instruction; store_lib.rs was audited at M1, so this is a newly discovered defect in an audited file. Proposed repair: set fetched_loader to NULL after ossl_store_close_it at the err tail (or free only in the loader_ctx == NULL branch), keeping the authority's non-double-release intent; control: allocator-refusal probe asserting one release and a live cache entry, then a cache flush.
